text:
maria_oncall: getting alerts for ap-northeast1 nodes, scheduling throttles kicking in around 11:12 UTC. GPU queue times spiking, some Pod evictions. looking now

raj_sre: confirmed — kube-scheduler shows backpressure, device plugin logs have repeated `failed to allocate` OOM traces. error rate ~4.8% over last 5m.

claire_ic: incident declared. assigning roles: raj SRE IC for remediation, maria incident comms. 

maria_oncall: rolling customer communication draft below, please review before I push to status page and Support playbook. short window ETA?

kevin_support: support brief: we already have 6 active tickets referencing timeouts in apac region. customers asking for ETA and failover options.

raj_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon bad nodes and drain gradually 2) spin up replacement A100 nodes in ap-east-1 (quota pending) 3) traffic-shift non-latency-critical workloads to us-east1 via GCLB header routing.

maria_oncall: thanks. can we get a quick ETA for option 2 (provision replacements)?

raj_sre: provisioning request to cloud team submitted (internal req #INC-4821). if quotas approved, new nodes will be ready in ~28-40 minutes. if quotas denied, fallback to shifting to us-east1 which is ~10-15m to flip routing rules.

claire_ic: priority: reduce customer impact. traffic shift first, then add capacity if available. mari, draft status update with both options and an ETA window. set expectation: degraded perf for APAC while we move traffic.

maria_oncall: draft status update (for status.redwood.ai):

"We are investigating increased GPU scheduling delays in ap-northeast1 impacting some requests. Engineers are actively shifting non-critical traffic to us-east1 and provisioning replacement capacity. Estimated restoration time 30-90 minutes. We will post updates every 10 minutes. If you see persistent errors, please contact support with your request ID."

kevin_support: good. add note about support tickets getting prioritized and temporary best-effort fallback to CPU models if latency is acceptable for the customer.

maria_oncall: updated draft includes CPU fallback option. preparing to publish. statusbot, please trigger an initial incident post.

statusbot: [automated] Incident posted to status.redwood.ai: "APAC GPU scheduling throttles affecting some requests in ap-northeast1". Next update scheduled in 10m.

tariq_prod: quick ask: any risk that routing to us-east1 will blow up token costs or latency SLAs? need to flag to sales for customers on strict SLAs.

raj_sre: yes — cross-region will add ~12-25ms median latency for APAC customers and increase egress costs. I'll add cost delta estimate to the incident notes.

sophia_cs: I'll start outreach to top 10 impacted customers, include ETA and mitigation steps (CPU fallback, regional failover). cc kevin_support.

maria_oncall: action list captured: 
- raj_sre: continue cordon/drain and initiate GCLB header routing change (in-progress)
- raj_sre: wait for quota approval for new A100s (INC-4821)
- kevin_support & sophia_cs: customer outreach and ticket prioritization
- statusbot: status page cadence every 10m

raj_sre: started header routing flip for non-critical traffic. running canary at 11:28 UTC (5% traffic).

kevin_support: can we tag which customers were moved to fallback CPU so support notes are clear?

raj_sre: yes, I'll annotate requests with `x-failover: cpu` header so logs/showback match.

maria_oncall: publishing follow-up update now: "We have shifted a subset of traffic to an alternate region and prioritized customer tickets. Engineers are also provisioning replacement GPUs; restoration still estimated 30-90 minutes."

statusbot: [automated] Status updated at 11:34 UTC.

claire_ic: escalation check: any customers with SLA breaches yet?

kevin_support: two affected customers on enterprise plans have reported timeouts; we're offering proactive credits and temporary routing to dedicated capacity where available.

raj_sre: can confirm canary looks healthy, latency delta acceptable for the canary cohort. proceeding to 30% traffic shift at 11:42 UTC.

maria_oncall: great. next update scheduled 11:44 UTC. if we have capacity online sooner we'll update ETA earlier.

sophia_cs: outreach messages sent to top 10 impacted, some asked for hard ETA. i'll cite 30-90m and mention proactive credits.

claire_ic: for postmortem: capture root cause (driver oom vs scheduling), timeline of failing nodes, decision to shift traffic, and cost implications. raj, please capture steps and RAW logs.

raj_sre: logging full driver traces to S3 under s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765123456/driver-traces.log. attaching ticket INC-4821 for provisioning.

maria_oncall: last note before next update: internal channel for this incident #inc-1765123456. please post any customer replies here so we can track communications.

statusbot: [automated] Next status update scheduled in 10 minutes.

kevin_support: ping when traffic shift completes so support can mark tickets as mitigated.

raj_sre: 11:58 UTC — traffic shift to us-east1 at 100% for non-latency workloads complete, evictions stopped on remaining nodes. starting validation run for latency-sensitive routes.

maria_oncall: published final interim update: "Most non-latency workloads have been shifted to an alternate region; evictions have stopped. We continue to validate latency-sensitive routing and provision replacement GPUs. Expected full recovery depends on quota approval."

claire_ic: holding for next steps. good job team.

kevin_support: closing loop with affected customers now. will open follow-up tickets for credits and SLA remediation.

sophia_cs: thanks everyone — I'll prepare the initial customer-facing RCA summary once we have the root cause and timeline.
